q: The position-based quantum cryptography (Malaney, Chandran-Fehr-Garg-Ostrovsky 2009) proposes using location as a cryptographic credential. Its security in the quantum setting:
opts: Can be broken by adversaries using quantum entanglement (port-based teleportation allows attacks)
Requires no quantum entanglement to attack
Is equivalent to quantum key distribution
exp: Position-based quantum cryptography is insecure against quantum adversaries who pre-share entangled states. Using port-based teleportation (Ishizaka-Hiroshima), the adversary can simulate the honest prover's actions. The attack uses O(d^4) EPR pairs for d-dimensional systems.
